findings.issue_text: **`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101` — the zod *result wrapper* is persisted as the credential key.**
**`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — `prisma` is not imported.**
**`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27` — placeholder `"refresh_token"` string overwrites real refresh tokens.**

When the parsed data lacks `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string `"refresh_token"`. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-272` the result is spread over `o365AuthCredentials` and written to the DB, so a refresh response without a `refresh_token` field (or one stripped by the sync-mode minimum schema, which only keeps `access_token`) permanently replaces the valid refresh token with garbage. The credential is then unrecoverable. Fix: only set fields that were actually returned, and preserve the existing refresh token explicitly (as the Salesforce path does at line 98).
**`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15` — the sync path returns a `Response`, but half the callers expect a parsed object.**
**`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-57` — the team branch returns before the admin check.**
**`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29` — auth bypass when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset.**
**`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11` — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not do what the comments say.**
**`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-108` — the refresh is unconditional and its result is discarded.**

**`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` — `response.statusText !== "OK"` is not a reliable success test.** HTTP/2 responses carry an empty `statusText`, so healthy refreshes throw a 400 with an empty message. Use `if (!response.ok)`.

**`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15` — the outbound sync request is unauthenticated and unchecked.** No secret header (the inbound direction has one), no `response.ok` check, no timeout. A non-2xx sync endpoint response flows onward as if it were a token. At minimum send `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and reject non-OK responses.

**`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31, 59-61` — unhandled throws become 500s.** `schema.parse` on a bad body throws `ZodError`, and `symmetricDecrypt` + `JSON.parse` throw on a wrong key or malformed ciphertext. All three should be `safeParse`/try-catch returning 400. There is also no HTTP method guard, so `GET`/`DELETE` reach the same handler.

**`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264` — diagnostics removed without replacement.** The previous `console.error` with the zod error and the raw MS response was deleted; the helper now throws a generic `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` with no context, making sync-mode failures very hard to debug. Also, `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` (and the identical check in Salesforce at line 92) is dead code, since the helper throws on failure.

**No tests.** Nothing covers the new webhook (secret mismatch, unknown user/app, bad ciphertext, create vs. update), `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens` branch selection, or the team-vs-user credential paths. Issues 1, 3 and 4 are exactly the kind a single round-trip test per app would have caught.

`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` — `appConfig.slug` was replaced with a hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"` while `appConfig.slug` is still used on line 12. Unrelated to the PR intent and a small regression in DRY-ness; revert it.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16` — stray empty `/** */` JSDoc.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:63-92` — `findFirst` + `update`/`create` is racy under concurrent pushes for the same `(userId, appId)`; a unique constraint plus `upsert`, or a transaction, would be safer. Also the endpoint has no rate limiting and supports only user (not team) credentials, with no delete/revoke path.
`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42` — `members: { select: { userId: true } }` is selected but never used.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9` — `JSON.parse` on attacker-controlled `req.query.state` with an unchecked cast to `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState`; a malformed state 500s, and `teamId` is trusted as-is by `createOAuthAppCredential`. Pre-existing behavior carried over by the move, but worth a zod schema now that it gates team credential creation.
`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts` — parse-then-stringify is a no-op round trip; also pre-existing.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

**`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11` — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not do what the comments say.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are evaluated immediately to *single literal property names* (e.g., "ZodString" / "[object Object]") in the JS object literal, not to “any string key”. So the schema does **not** mean “any numeric property is expiry” nor “allow other properties”. It will instead define (at most) one specific key twice (likely overwriting one), making the schema behavior incorrect relative to the comments and intent. The proper way would be something like `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).catchall(z.unknown())` (and separately validate expiry fields) or use `z.record(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:63-92` — `findFirst` + `update`/`create` is racy under concurrent pushes for the same `(userId, appId)`; a unique constraint plus `upsert`, or a transaction, would be safer. Also the endpoint has no rate limiting and supports only user (not team) credentials, with no delete/revoke path.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler does a non-atomic read-then-write sequence: it calls `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and then either `update` or `create` based on the result. Under concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)`, both requests can observe “no row” and both attempt `create`, causing either duplicate credentials (if there’s no DB uniqueness) or a thrown unique-constraint error/500 (if there is). This is a real correctness/concurrency issue introduced by the diff and would be avoided with a transaction or an `upsert` keyed by a unique constraint. The additional comments about lack of rate limiting / no revoke path are more design/security hardening suggestions than strictly verifiable defects, but the race condition itself is clearly present.
